newsitem.title: USA: Rhode Island rape-charge mayor loses election.
newsitem.headline: Rhode Island rape-charge mayor loses election.

text.p: The mayor of a tiny resort island accused of taking part in a gang rape lost his bid for re-election, town officials said on Wednesday.

Edward McGovern, a 48-year-old Democrat, was soundly defeated by last-minute write-in candidate Kim Gaffett, a Republican. Gaffett, 39, beat McGovern by 488 votes to 270, a spokeswoman in the town clerk's office told Reuters.

McGovern and two other men were charged last month with raping a 21-year-old waitress on Oct. 6 in a bar owned by McGovern. McGovern, who denies the rape charge, said in a statement published in the Block Island Times newspaper last month: "I do not intend to be chased from office on false allegations or unfair rumours or innuendo."
The case was expected to go before a grand jury, town officials said.
McGovern had been First Warden, or mayor, for eight years in the tourist-dependent island of 800 year-round residents. Calls for his resignation began shortly after the rape charge was filed.
Voter turnout on Tuesday was higher than usual, and "There is a sense of relief (that McGovern lost)," said Katie Mulvaney, managing editor of the Block Island Times.
Gaffett, to be sworn in in early December, said she entered the race because McGovern was running unopposed. "I thought maybe the island should have a choice," she said.
